findings.name: Total Property Tax Exemption for 100% Permanent Service-Connected Disability
findings.description: Homestead property owned and used by an honorably discharged veteran with a VA-certified service-connected total and permanent disability is fully exempt from ad valorem property taxes. The exemption continues for an unremarried surviving spouse who holds title and permanently resides on the homestead.
findings.value: Full exemption from ad valorem taxes on homestead property
otherReqs: Permanent Florida resident on January 1 of the tax year (or on January 1 of the year of death for surviving spouse)
Property must be owned and used as a homestead
VA letter certifying total and permanent disability
documentation: VA letter of total and permanent disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Any real estate that is owned and used as a homestead by a veteran who was honorably discharged with a service-connected total and permanent disability... The production by a veteran or the spouse...of a letter of total and permanent disability [is prima facie evidence]. A veteran must be a permanent resident of this state on January 1 of the tax year for which exemption is being claimed, or on January 1 of the year the veteran died.

findings.name: $5,000 Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Ex-Servicemembers
findings.description: Ex-servicemembers disabled to a degree of 10 percent or more by misfortune, or while serving during wartime, are entitled to a $5,000 exemption from the taxable value of their property. An unremarried surviving spouse of such a disabled ex-servicemember is also entitled to the exemption.
otherReqs: Disability rated 10% or more (misfortune or wartime service)
documentation: Certificate of disability from the U.S. Government or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
findings.sourceExcerpt: disabled to a degree of 10 percent or more by misfortune or while serving during a period of wartime service... Property to the value of $5,000 of such a person is exempt from taxation... The unremarried surviving spouse of such a disabled ex-servicemember is also entitled to the exemption.

findings.name: Homestead Tax Discount for Veterans Age 65+ with Combat-Related Disability
findings.description: Veterans age 65 or older who are partially or totally permanently disabled, where the disability is combat-related and the veteran was honorably discharged, receive a discount on homestead ad valorem taxes equal to the percentage of their VA-rated permanent service-connected disability. A surviving spouse may retain the discount if they hold title and permanently reside on the homestead.
findings.value: Discount percentage equal to the VA service-connected disability rating percentage
otherReqs: Own and reside on homestead property
Application to county property appraiser due by March 1
findings.form: DR-501DV (Application and Return for Homestead Tax Discount - Veterans Age 65 and Older with a Combat-Related Disability)
documentation: Official VA correspondence confirming disability percentage
Proof of age as of January 1
findings.sourceExcerpt: Each veteran who is age 65 or older and is partially or totally permanently disabled shall receive a discount... The discount shall be in a percentage equal to the percentage of the veteran's permanent, service-connected disability as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs.

findings.name: Florida State Veterans' Nursing Homes (Veterans' Nursing Home of Florida Act)
findings.description: Florida operates a network of state veterans' nursing homes under the Veterans' Nursing Home of Florida Act (Chapter 296, Part II), providing skilled nursing and long-term care to eligible veterans. Admission requires need of nursing home care, Florida residency at time of application, no outstanding debt to the department, application for all available governmental financial assistance, and VA approval. Priority is given first to Florida residents, then to veterans with VA-determined service-connected disabilities, then to veterans with non-service-connected disabilities who cannot afford care.
findings.value: Access to state-operated skilled nursing home care
otherReqs: Florida resident at time of application (waivable for disaster evacuees from a state under declared emergency)
No outstanding debt to the Department of Veterans' Affairs
Application for all available governmental financial assistance
documentation: VA approval/certification of need for nursing home care
findings.legalCitation: Florida Statutes §296.31-296.41 (Veterans' Nursing Home of Florida Act), specifically §296.36
findings.sourceExcerpt: Priority... 1. Florida residents - eligible veterans residing in the state. 2. Service-connected disability - veterans with VA-determined service-connected disabilities or those discharged for disability incurred in line of duty. 3. Non-service-connected disability - veterans unable to afford care who swear under oath before a notary. The director may waive residency requirements for a veteran who is a disaster evacuee of a state that is under a declared state of emergency.

findings.name: Congressman C.W. "Bill" Young Veteran Tuition Waiver Program
findings.description: Florida state universities, Florida College System institutions, and career centers may waive out-of-state tuition fees so that qualifying veterans (and certain VA education-benefit users) pay no more than in-state resident tuition and fees, regardless of Florida residency length. Applies to honorably discharged veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces, Reserve Forces, or National Guard who physically reside in Florida while enrolled, and to those entitled to and using VA educational assistance for terms beginning after July 1, 2015 who physically reside in Florida while enrolled.
findings.value: Waiver of out-of-state tuition fees; tuition/fees capped at in-state resident rate
otherReqs: Enrollment at a state university, Florida College System institution, or career center
findings.agency: State university / Florida College System institution / career center (individual institution administers waiver); reporting to Board of Governors and State Board of Education
documentation: Proof of honorable discharge or documentation of VA educational assistance entitlement
findings.sourceExcerpt: An honorably discharged veteran of the United States Armed Forces, the United States Reserve Forces, or the National Guard who physically resides in this state... [or one who] is entitled to and uses educational assistance provided by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs [for a term beginning after July 1, 2015] who physically resides in this state while enrolled... may be cited as the 'Congressman C.W. "Bill" Young Veteran Tuition Waiver Act.'

findings.name: Florida Veterans' Preference in Employment
findings.description: The State of Florida and its political subdivisions must give preference in appointment and retention in positions of employment to disabled veterans, spouses of totally disabled or missing/captured veterans, survivors of veterans who died of service-connected causes, wartime veterans, all honorably discharged veterans, and current reserve/National Guard members. The Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs adopts rules implementing point values (per s. 295.08) or special-consideration procedures at each step of hiring.
findings.value: Statutory hiring/retention preference in state and local government employment
otherReqs: Applies to state and political subdivision employment; certain elected, temporary, and Bar-membership positions are exempt
findings.agency: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs (rulemaking); individual state/local government employers (implementation)
documentation: VA disability rating letter (for disabled veteran preference category)
findings.sourceExcerpt: the state and its political subdivisions shall give preference in appointment and retention in positions of employment [to disabled veterans, spouses of totally disabled veterans or those missing in action/captured, survivors of veterans who died from service-connected disabilities, wartime veterans, all veterans with honorable discharge, and current reserve/National Guard members]... rules...must include the award of point values as articulated in s. 295.08, if applicable, or...must include procedures to ensure that veterans are given special consideration at each step of the employment selection process.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran ("DV") License Plate
findings.description: Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 100 percent are eligible for a permanent "DV" license plate, issued at no charge to the applicant (only the standard statutory service charge and the 50-cent fee under s. 320.084 apply, not the base plate fee). The plate displays red, white, and blue colors similar to the U.S. flag. Eligible veterans may instead choose a military or specialty plate, but must pay applicable fees for those alternatives.
findings.value: Free permanent DV license plate (no charge to applicant)
findings.agency: Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV)
documentation: Letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (or predecessor agency/uniformed service branch) certifying a service-connected disability rating of 100 percent
findings.sourceExcerpt: service-connected 100-percent disability rating for compensation... One free motor vehicle license number plate shall be issued by the department... The production by a veteran of a valid identification card issued by the Department of Veterans' Affairs...or a letter from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs...certifying a service-connected disability rating of 100 percent for the veteran is prima facie evidence of the veteran's eligibility... the department is authorized to issue a designation plate containing only the letters 'DV,' to be displayed on the front.
